title: Role of Heat Treatment Atmosphere on the Microstructure and Surface Morphology of DLP-Fabricated High-Entropy Alloy Components.

recollection.starting_material: DLP-printed high-entropy alloy green parts composed of a powder/resin slurry, probably a CoCrFeNi or similar equiatomic HEA system
recollection.intervention: Post-printing heat treatments carried out in different atmospheres (vacuum, flowing Ar, N2, and air; possibly also H2–Ar)
recollection.structure: Vacuum/Ar produced a single-phase FCC HEA with fine equiaxed grains and low surface roughness, whereas air led to an outer oxide layer (~5–10 µm) and coarser, partially recrystallised grains; H2-containing atmospheres yielded the smoothest, densest surface with minimal porosity
recollection.mechanism: Atmosphere controlled the extent of oxidation and evaporation of minor elements during heating; inert or reducing gases suppressed oxide scale formation and enabled surface diffusion and grain refinement, while air promoted oxidation, grain growth, and surface roughening
recollection.results: Best condition (H2–Ar, 1100 °C, 1 h) gave relative density >99.5 %, average grain size ~8 µm, surface roughness (Ra) ~1.2 µm, and hardness ~550 HV; air-treated samples showed density 96 %, grain size >25 µm, Ra ~6 µm, and hardness dropped to ~430 HV

score.note: The recollection only broadly captures that air versus oxygen-deficient/inert conditions affect oxidation during heat treatment. It invents Ar, N2, H2–Ar, phase/grain/roughness outcomes, and density/hardness values. It misses the key residual-carbon, gas-evolution, cracking, oxide-limited diffusion mechanism, the 1050 versus 1100 °C consolidation shift, and the reported oxygen/carbon contents and strengths.
